relevance_reason: The paper reports a stillborn case of SMABF2 with compound heterozygous ASCC1 variants (an exonic microdeletion and a nonsense variant) and describes how the disease developed before birth.

findings.statement: Giuffrida et al. (2020) described the first case of SMABF2 diagnosed in a stillbirth, in which the course of the disease was documented during the prenatal period. Arthrogryposis and hydrops were present, and these findings prompted chromosomal microarray analysis.
quotes: This work describes the first case of SMABF2 in a stillbirth with documented evolution of the disease in the prenatal period.
was firstly detected by microarray analysis, requested for arthrogryposis and hydrops

findings.statement: In a stillborn fetus with SMABF2, Giuffrida et al. (2020) found compound heterozygous variants in the ASCC1 gene. Microarray analysis first detected a microdeletion of about 64 kb that involved 4 exons of ASCC1. Exome analysis then identified a c.1027C>T nonsense variant (Arg343Ter) that introduces a premature termination codon. The authors stated that this was the first reported case of ASCC1 compound heterozygosity caused by an exonic microdeletion together with a nucleotide variant.
quotes: A microdeletion copy number variant (CNV) of about 64 Kb, involving four exons of ASCC1, was firstly detected by microarray analysis
Subsequent exome analysis disclosed a nucleotide variant of the same gene [c.1027C>T; (p. Arg343*)], resulting in the introduction of a premature termination codon.
This stillbirth represents the first case of ASCC1 compound heterozygosity, due to an exonic microdeletion and a nucleotide variant

variants.as_reported: microdeletion copy number variant (CNV) of about 64 Kb, involving four exons of ASCC1

relevance_reason: Reports three additional families with ASCC1 mutations causing prenatal-onset muscle weakness, arthrogryposis and congenital bone fractures (SMABF2).

findings.statement: Böhm et al. (2019) provided a clinical, histological and genetic description of 3 families with ASCC1-related disorder. All patients presented with severe prenatal-onset muscle weakness, neonatal hypotonia, arthrogryposis, and congenital bone fractures.
quotes: Here, we provide a clinical, histological and genetic description of three additional ASCC1 families.
All patients presented with severe prenatal-onset muscle weakness, neonatal hypotonia and arthrogryposis, and congenital bone fractures.

findings.statement: Böhm et al. (2019) found that muscle biopsies from affected infants showed intense oxidative rims beneath the sarcolemma and scattered remnants of sarcomeres with enlarged Z-bands, which the authors suggested could represent a histopathologic hallmark of the disorder.
quotes: The muscle biopsies from the affected infants revealed intense oxidative rims beneath the sarcolemma and scattered remnants of sarcomeres with enlarged Z-bands, potentially representing a histopathological hallmark of the disorder.

phenotypes.text: subsarcolemmal oxidative rims on muscle biopsy

findings.statement: In affected individuals from 3 families with prenatal-onset muscle weakness, arthrogryposis and congenital bone fractures, Böhm et al. (2019) identified recessive nonsense or frameshift mutations in the ASCC1 gene by sequencing, including 2 novel mutations.
quotes: Sequencing identified recessive nonsense or frameshift mutations in ASCC1, including two novel mutations.

relevance_reason: The paper reports a second family with SMABF2 that carries a homozygous ASCC1 frameshift variant, which confirms that ASCC1 is involved in the disorder.

findings.statement: Oliveira et al. (2017) described a female newborn with a severe neuromuscular disorder. She had generalized hypotonia, congenital bone fractures, no spontaneous movements and poor respiratory effort, and she died within the first days of life. A male sib born later had the same clinical presentation. Karyotyping and screening of several neuromuscular disease genes were negative.
quotes: The patient presented generalized hypotonia, congenital bone fractures, lack of spontaneous movements and poor respiratory effort. She died within the first days of life.
A male sibling was subsequently born with the same clinical presentation.

phenotypes.text: death in first days of life

findings.statement: Whole-exome sequencing under a recessive model first found no disease-causing variants in known neuromuscular genes. Oliveira et al. (2017) then identified a homozygous frameshift variant in the ASCC1 gene (c.157dupG, p.Glu53Glyfs*19) in the female proband. The authors concluded that this second known case confirms ASCC1 involvement in a severe neuromuscular disease lying within the spinal muscular atrophy or primary muscle disease spectra.
quotes: Our patient was also found to have a homozygous frameshift variant (c.157dupG, p.Glu53Glyfs*19) in ASCC1 , thereby representing the second known case.
This confirms ASCC1 involvement in a severe neuromuscular disease lying within the spinal muscular atrophy or primary muscle disease spectra.

relevance_reason: Reports recessive loss-of-function ASCC1 (and TRIP4) mutations in families with prenatal-onset SMA and congenital bone fractures, plus functional studies including zebrafish knockdown and patient fibroblast expression changes.

findings.statement: Knierim et al. (2016) studied 4 families in which affected individuals presented with prenatal-onset spinal muscular atrophy, multiple congenital contractures (arthrogryposis multiplex congenita), respiratory distress, and congenital bone fractures.
quotes: We used autozygosity mapping and whole-exome sequencing to search for pathogenic mutations in four families.

Affected individuals presented with prenatal-onset spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), multiple congenital contractures (arthrogryposis multiplex congenita), respiratory distress, and congenital bone fractures.

findings.statement: In affected individuals from 4 families with prenatal-onset SMA and congenital bone fractures, Knierim et al. (2016) used autozygosity mapping and whole-exome sequencing to identify homozygous and compound heterozygous nonsense and frameshift mutations in the TRIP4 and ASCC1 genes, encoding subunits of the nuclear activating signal cointegrator 1 (ASC-1) complex. The mutations cosegregated with the disease and led to truncation or entire absence of the respective proteins.
quotes: We report on recessive loss-of-function mutations in two genes (TRIP4 and ASCC1) that encode subunits of the nuclear activating signal cointegrator 1 (ASC-1) complex.

We identified homozygous and compound-heterozygous nonsense and frameshift TRIP4 and ASCC1 mutations that led to a truncation or the entire absence of the respective proteins and cosegregated with the disease phenotype.

findings.statement: Knierim et al. (2016) found that the phenotype of prenatal-onset SMA with congenital bone fractures was associated with mutations in either of 2 genes, TRIP4 or ASCC1, both encoding subunits of the ASC-1 complex.
quotes: We report on recessive loss-of-function mutations in two genes (TRIP4 and ASCC1) that encode subunits of the nuclear activating signal cointegrator 1 (ASC-1) complex.

findings.statement: Knierim et al. (2016) found that morpholino knockdown of either trip4 or ascc1 in zebrafish disrupted alpha-motoneuron outgrowth and formation of myotomes and neuromuscular junctions and caused a swimming defect in larvae.
quotes: Antisense morpholino-mediated knockdown of either trip4 or ascc1 in zebrafish disrupted the highly patterned and coordinated process of α-motoneuron outgrowth and formation of myotomes and neuromuscular junctions and led to a swimming defect in the larvae.

findings.statement: Knierim et al. (2016) found that ASCC1 mutant patient fibroblasts downregulated genes associated with neurogenesis, neuronal migration, and pathfinding (SERPINF1, DAB1, SEMA3D, SEMA3A) and with bone development (TNFRSF11B, RASSF2, STC1). Immunoprecipitation of the ASC-1 complex consistently copurified the transcriptional cofactor CSRP1. The authors concluded that dysfunction of a transcriptional coactivator complex can result in a syndrome affecting the neuromuscular system.
quotes: ASCC1 mutant fibroblasts downregulated genes associated with neurogenesis, neuronal migration, and pathfinding (SERPINF1, DAB1, SEMA3D, SEMA3A), as well as with bone development (TNFRSF11B, RASSF2, STC1).
Immunoprecipitation of the ASC-1 complex consistently copurified cysteine and glycine rich protein 1 (CSRP1), a transcriptional cofactor
Our findings indicate that the dysfunction of a transcriptional coactivator complex can result in a clinical syndrome affecting the neuromuscular system.

findings.statement: Knierim et al. (2016) found that Trip4 and Ascc1 had identical expression patterns in embryonic day 17.5 mouse embryos, with high expression in spinal cord, brain, paraspinal ganglia, thyroid, and submandibular glands.
quotes: Trip4 and Ascc1 have identical expression patterns in 17.5-day-old mouse embryos with high expression levels in the spinal cord, brain, paraspinal ganglia, thyroid, and submandibular glands.
